NO OFFENSE: Civil Religion and Protestant Taste

by John Murray Cuddihy ‧ RELEASE DATE: March 1, 1978
Cuddihy rides again, rumbling through the china shop of academic sociology. This lively, controversial thinker, whose Ordeal of Civility (1974) claimed that the thought of Marx, Freud, and Levi-Strauss was rooted in Jewish ""resentment"" of modernity, returns to study the conflict between religious communities and secularist society--this time in America. Cuddihy approaches the problem through the life and work of three major figures, Reinhold Niebuhr, Father John Courtney Murray, and Rabbi Arthur Hertzberg. His thesis, briefly, is that European religion and politics too, though he treats this as an afterthought--undergoes a transformation, a ""taming and assimilation,"" beneath American skies.
